settings.desc.title: Description text
settings.desc.intro: What gets appended to the Strava activity description. Pick a preset to start from, or write your own (Go text/template syntax: {{.TIR}}, {{.TIRWindow}}, {{.TIRBar}}, {{.TIRWindowBar}}, {{.Min}}, {{.Max}}, {{.Avg}}, {{.StdDev}}, {{.CV}}, {{.GMI}}, {{.VeryLow}}, {{.VeryHigh}}, {{.Unit}}, {{.Distance}}, {{.Elevation}}, {{.Pace}}, {{.Sparkline}}; {{if .Sparkline}}...{{end}} to only show a line when it's there). {{.TIR}} is the activity window; {{.TIRWindow}} is the wider pre/post window the chart draws from below, so the two can differ — add both if you want to show that. {{.Pace}} is a single field that's already the right unit for the activity's sport (pace for a run/hike/walk/swim, speed for a ride), empty when there's no meaningful distance metric for the sport. The preview below updates as you type, using your latest activity or sample data.

strava.login.warning: Unverified against the real Strava login form. It gives up at the first CAPTCHA, verification code or wrong-password message and never guesses past one; nothing is stored unless it reaches your dashboard. If it fails, use cookie import below instead. Strava may notice a new sign-in and email you about it, same as any other browser login.

strava.import.intro: Log in to strava.com in your browser, export the cookies for strava.com, and paste them here. Three formats work:

strava.import.help: Stored encrypted. Only the cookie names are ever shown again.
strava.process.title: Process a specific activity
strava.process.intro: Write the glucose description onto an activity that was never auto-detected, for example one from before glucava was running, or older than the polling window. It is looked up in your Strava training log if it isn't already known here.

strava.process.help: The number at the end of the activity's URL on strava.com.
strava.good.title: Good to know
strava.good.tos: Automating the Strava website goes against Strava's terms of service. glucava uses one browser, one account and a few page loads per activity. Use it at your own risk.
strava.good.cookies: Treat these cookies like a password: anyone who has them is logged in as you. Log out of the browser session you exported from only if you want to invalidate them.
strava.good.expiry: When Strava ends the session, you get a notification and need to import fresh cookies.

tokens.reveal.hint: A working call answers 202, and “Last used” in the list below changes.
tokens.tasker.title: Android (Tasker)
tokens.tasker.intro: A ready-to-import profile: Strava notification → check now, unfiltered (see below for why).

tokens.other.title: Other platforms
tokens.other.intro: Scan to open this page on the phone you'll set the trigger up on — the instructions below fill in this real token instead of a placeholder.
tokens.other.qr: QR code to open the Triggers page
tokens.how.title: How to call it
tokens.how.intro: Send a POST request with the token. The call only asks glucava to check Strava now; it carries no other data. “Last used” in the list above shows whether your phone's call arrived.
tokens.how.android.title: Android (Tasker)
tokens.how.android.1: Task: Net → HTTP Request. Method POST, URL and header as above, empty body, timeout 30. Run it once by hand and check “Last used”.
tokens.how.android.2: Profile: Event → UI → Notification, owner application Strava, no filter yet. Link it to the task.
tokens.how.android.3: After Strava's next “activity saved” notification, look at Tasker's run log. If the profile also fires for kudos or comments, add a title or text filter with the wording you see there.
tokens.how.android.4: Tasker needs notification access and unrestricted battery use.
tokens.how.android.other: HTTP Shortcuts and MacroDroid work the same way: trigger on a Strava notification, then send the request.
tokens.how.iphone.title: iPhone (Shortcuts)
tokens.how.iphone.body: Personal automation → Workout → Ends (or App → Strava → Is Closed), set to Run Immediately. Actions: Wait 30 seconds, then Get Contents of URL with method POST and the header above. iOS cannot react to another app's notification. This has not been tested yet.
tokens.how.fallback: Without any trigger, polling still picks up new activities on the interval from Settings.

validate.unit: Unit must be mg/dL or mmol/L.
validate.range_low: Target low must be between 40 and 200 mg/dL.
validate.range_high: Target high must be above the low value and at most 400 mg/dL.
validate.thresholds: Very low must be between 20 and the target low, and very high between the target high and 600 mg/dL.
validate.minutes: Minutes before and after must be between 0 and 240.
validate.chart_theme: Chart theme must be light or dark.
validate.chart_size: Chart size must be standard or large.
validate.chart_lead: Chart lead-in must be between 0 and 240 minutes.
validate.chart_line: Chart line thickness must be between 1 and 4.
validate.poll: The polling interval must be between 1 and 1440 minutes.
validate.post_buffer: The delayed reprocess buffer must be between 0 and 180 minutes.
validate.retention: Retention must be between 0 and 3650 days.
validate.ntfy_url: The ntfy URL must start with http:// or https://.
validate.webhook_url: The webhook URL must start with http:// or https://.
validate.email_to: The notification email address is not valid.
validate.smtp_port: The SMTP port must be between 1 and 65535.
validate.smtp_sender: The SMTP sender address is not valid.
validate.gap_alert: The glucose gap alert must be between 0 and 168 hours.
validate.public_url: The public URL must start with http:// or https://.
validate.smtp_needs: SMTP needs a port and a sender address.
validate.panel_order: Chart panel order must only list activity, band, dots, hr.
validate.language: Language must be auto or one of the installed languages.
validate.artifact_mode: Suspected artifacts must be handled as flagged or exclude.
validate.overview_range: The default Overview range must be one of {ranges}.
validate.overview_layout: The Overview layout is not valid JSON: {error}
